decisions.reason: Superyacht crew recruitment remains a close adjacent use of the firm's maritime crewing, training and network capabilities, so absorptive capacity is high and the offer can be improved without major capability stretch.

The maritime education programme fits the firm's existing training centres, crewing base and institutional partnerships, and the early expansion to six partner institutions shows learnable traction in an area the firm already understands well.

Emissions monitoring and compliance services are highly related to the firm's compliance-focused ship management activities, and the successful on-time submission of all FuelEU plans indicates strong execution and scope to commercialise accumulated regulatory know-how.

The emissions compliance dashboard builds directly on the firm's software and ship-management knowledge, and its integration into PAL makes it easier for the firm to absorb client feedback and refine the product as part of the core service stack.

The emissions compliance cost simulation tool also leverages the firm's digital and regulatory capabilities, but as a newer decision-support product its market learning is slightly less proven than the service-led compliance offer, so withdrawal risk is somewhat higher though still low.
